requirement.description: The Tags class constructor does not properly raise TypeError for invalid input types. Specifically, when passed single string or integer arguments (like Tags("tag") or Tags(1)), it should raise TypeError but currently doesn't.
requirement.contract: The Tags class constructor must raise TypeError when called with invalid argument types that are not dicts, AWSHelperFn instances, or keyword arguments. Valid calls include: Tags(key="value"), Tags({"key": "value"}), Tags(some_aws_helper_fn), Tags(key1="value1", key2="value2"). Invalid calls that should raise TypeError include: Tags("tag"), Tags(1), Tags("key", "value"), Tags({}, "key", "value").

requirement.description: The Tags class constructor does not properly validate positional arguments that should raise TypeError. When passed positional arguments that aren't dictionaries or AWSHelperFn instances, it should raise TypeError but currently allows them through.
requirement.contract: The Tags class constructor must validate all positional arguments and raise TypeError for unsupported types. Specifically, when a single positional argument is passed that is not a dict or AWSHelperFn, it should raise TypeError. This applies to cases like Tags("key", "value") or Tags(1) which should raise TypeError.

requirement.description: The Tags class constructor does not properly validate positional arguments that should raise TypeError. When passed multiple positional arguments, it should raise TypeError but currently allows them through.
requirement.contract: The Tags class constructor must validate all positional arguments and raise TypeError for unsupported types. Specifically, when multiple positional arguments are passed, it should raise TypeError. This applies to cases like Tags("key", "value") which should raise TypeError.
